answer: Aging-based trust resists Sybil attacks: every new identity starts with zero weight, and influence grows only through a long, verifiable history of honest service — each completed task adds a small pulse of reputation, like a ripple spreading slowly outward. An attacker can spawn a thousand aliases at dawn, but none can vote, earn, or attest until each has done months of real work, so faking influence costs exactly what doing the work for real costs.
